observations.finding: Control f_a63b63b85186: confluent monolayer of well spread cells. Nuclei (blue) uniformly oval, single per cell, smooth contour. Green tubulin forms fine filamentous network. Red F-actin thin at cell periphery. Few rounded bright cells. Treated fields f_a1de3dcad3cd, f_1b89888098c5 (0.03uM) and f_0072fc6616f9, f_5fdd58869bd8 (0.3uM) - markedly less confluent with large black background, same contrast. Read from colour composite only, no separate grayscale provided.

Blue DNA stain: treated nuclei irregular, multilobed, fragmented into grape-like clusters of multiple small micronuclei/puncta within one cytoplasm, plus enlarged irregular single nuclei vs control uniform ovals. Seen in all 4 fields, more extreme at 0.3uM.
Nuclear shape metrics strongly decreased - irregularity/multilobulation visible.
Fraction of enlarged nuclei visibly increased: many 2-4x larger lobated nuclei and poly-nuclear cells vs control rare.

Integrated DAPI brightness/DNA content increased: clusters of micronuclei and enlarged nuclei show more intense combined blue signal per cell than control; many small intensely DAPI-bright rounded mitotic-like cells (yellow-white overlap of blue+pink+green) scattered on surface, >10 per field vs 1-2 in control.

Red F-actin stain: visibly brighter, thicker peripheral ruffles and stress fibres, larger inter-cell variation in red intensity vs control faint uniform peripheral actin. At 0.3uM some star-like contracted actin halos around rounded cells.

Green tubulin still present, filamentous network visible, no global loss; red dominates over green vs control balanced green/red, indicating increased actin/tubulin ratio not tubulin depolymerization.
Cell rounding: numerous small bright round refractile yellow/pink cells on top of adherent cells, consistent with increased roundness, more numerous than control.
Reduced cell number/density in treated fields (sparse islands with empty space) vs dense control monolayer - not among measured features.

Specimen s_bb3b52891e unblinded as vincristine (PubChem CID 5978, ChEMBL CHEMBL90555 Tubulin inhibitor e19) - identity check agrees.

Reflection: Phenotype across 0.03-10 µM showed extreme nuclear irregularity (nuc_solidity z -30 to -46, nuc_form_factor z -23 to -34) with polyploidy/micronuclei (frac_large_nucleus z +9 to +21, nuc_dna_integrated z +6 to +14) plus dose-dependent cytoskeletal changes (tub_mean rho +1.0, act_std rho +1.0, tub_std z up to +21 at 10 µM). Microscopist favored Aurora kinase inhibitors based on multilobed/micronucleated morphology, but NSC vote was 3/4 Microtubule destabilizers with high cosine similarities 0.89-0.92 to demecolcine/nocodazole references (e6), outweighing single-model visual call. High-dose tubulin texture increase and cell loss consistent with microtubule destabilization leading to failed mitosis and secondary nuclear irregularity/polyploidy, correctly classified as Microtubule destabilizers.

Literature supports vinca alkaloids as microtubule depolymerizers/microtubule-targeting agents causing mitotic arrest: e.g., vincristine microtubule depolymerization susceptibility (PMID:35436470), TK216 microtubule targeting (PMID:35803262), mitotic inhibitors disrupting microtubule dynamics (PMID:27760837), and sensitization to microtubule-targeting agents (PMID:36967563).

reflection.text:
This run correctly called Microtubule destabilizers for vincristine and the unblinding confirms the call against ChEMBL Tubulin inhibitor annotation. What got it right was primarily the quantitative acquisition and atlas comparison, not the visual call.

What worked:
- Dosing strategy: starting from e1 (0.003-10 uM, 4 wells budget) we sampled 4 doses spanning onset to high: e4 0.03 uM, e2 0.3 uM, e5 1 uM, e3 10 uM. That showed the nuclear phenotype was already maximal at low dose (e4 nuc_solidity z=-33.4, nuc_form_factor z=-30.0, frac_large_nucleus z=+21.6; e2 nuc_solidity z=-43.8, form_factor -39.5; e5 solidity -46.6) and therefore dose_response for solidity was flat (e8 rho=+0.20 p=0.8). Acquiring the low dose was key - without e4 we could have mistaken this for a high-dose off-target effect.
- Atlas comparison e6: NSC 3/4 microtubule destabilizers, k-neighbours 6/10 destabilizers / 4/10 Eg5 inhibitors. This outweighed the competing visual signal and was correctly up-weighted in e16 (0.68 vs 0.22 Aurora, 0.10 Eg5) and e17 rationale.
- Cytoskeletal readouts at high dose: e3 tub_std z=+21.4 at 10 uM and the dose trajectories e10 tub_mean rho=+1.00 p=0 and e12 act_std rho=+1.00 p=0. With e14 cell_area rho=-0.80 were taken as destabilizer-consistent texture/collapse signature, and e5 act_std +16.2 at 1 uM supported it. Cell count drop 330 -> 130 cells from 0.03 to 10 uM across e4/e2/e5/e3 was also consistent with anti-mitotic toxicity.

What misled or was unresolved:
- Both describe_phenotype calls e7 and e15 returned Aurora kinase inhibitors candidates (9 and 5 observations, density lower vs DMSO). In isolation that pushed e16 Aurora to 0.22. Extreme nuclear irregularity (solidity -30 to -46) and frac_large_nucleus +14-21 plus e11 nuc_dna_integrated rho=+0.80 p=0.2 can be read as polyploidy/Aurora-like, and that is why Aurora was kept as alternate hypothesis. The atlas split with Eg5 4/10 in e6 shows Eg5 was a close neighbour for the same reason (monopolar/irregular nuclei overlapping phenotype).
- e8/e9 flat trajectories for solidity and frac_mitotic_like (rho 0.20 and 0.40, p 0.6-0.8) with only n=4 wells gave underpowered p-values, so we could not formally demonstrate dose-dependency of the mitotic arrest, only of tub/act texture. e13 cell_roundness rho=0.00 also did not support a clean rounding arrest curve.
- e10 tub_mean increasing with dose is counter-intuitive for a depolymerizer if interpreted as polymer mass; we interpreted e3 tub_std increase as texture/variance disruption rather than mean loss, which atlas voting supports but visual inspection e15 alone did not confirm as clear depolymerization.

Why the final weighting was justified: With n=4, direct similarity ranking (e6) is more robust than single-model textual labels from e7/e15. The combination of extreme solidity loss present already at 0.03 uM, large-nucleus fraction, cell loss at high dose, and tub/act texture dose dependence matches microtubule dysregulation leading to aberrant mitosis and micronucleation/large nuclei, not primary Aurora B inhibition, even though the nuclear morphology overlaps. ChEMBL lookup e18/e19 confirming vincristine as Tubulin inhibitor and literature search e20 (13 hits, 5 returned for vincristine tubulin inhibitor) aligned with this, as discussed for microtubule-targeting agents in this context e.g. PMID 35803262, PMID 27472259, PMID 35436470, PMID 27760837, PMID 36967563, without needing to invoke an Aurora mechanism.

Missed/limitations: No phospho-H3 or Aurora B substrate readout was available to directly exclude Aurora; e21 search for nuclear irregularity/polyploidy phenotype returned 0 hits, so we lacked literature comparator for morphology in-run. Future experiment as proposed (live tubulin polymerization + p-H3/Aurora B IF and DNA content flow vs reference destabilizer and Aurora inhibitor, with washout) would be required to functionally separate destabilizer-induced mitotic failure from Aurora inhibition.
